text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthWalking May Improve Your Attention SpanOne more reason to get those steps inJCBy Jake Currie6:00 PM CDT on October 19, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWalking is a great way to clear your head—or so anecdotes would have you believe. Now a new long-term study published in Scientific Reports is putting some intellectual heft behind this advice.    Powered By 10 ShareNextStayResearchers from the Baylor College of Medicine uncovered the relationship by analyzing 14 years of health data from more than 3,000 adults aged 18 to 93 as part of the NIH’s All of Us Research Program. The team relied on daily step counts recorded by FitBits monitors, rather than self-reported daily activity (which tends to be less accurate). Additionally, the participants took cognitive assessments to measure their sustained attention, cognitive control (the ability to filter out distractions), delay discounting (the ability to delay gratification), and emotion recognition (the ability to read facial expressions).Read more: “Here’s Why Our Walking Gets Slower as We Age”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
